rules_text:
Rules summary OVERVIEW Roll dice to collect items to show off on your 5x5 bookshelf...and as many points as possible! You must collect at least 3 items, or you won't score points for that row or column at all. If another player collects all 5 items in a row or column, though, no one else can claim anything in that row or column for the rest of the game. When any player has 2 rows filled - with treasures and/or X's - the game ends. GAME PLAY On your turn, roll all 6 dice. You may re-roll any number of dice twice after that. 5 sides of the die match a color/symbol on your bookshelf, and 1 side is a wild joker. Dice are turned in to collect (circle) items on your bookshelf based on color/symbol and number. EXAMPLE: 3 pink dice can be used together to circle the 3rd item in your pink row OR 1 pink die can be used to circle the 1st item in the pink row and the remaining 2 pink dice used together to circle the 2nd item in the pink row. You can circle up to 3 items on your turn. UNABLE TO CIRCLE ~ If you can't circle anything on your bookshelf, you must cross out an entire row of your choice! You cannot place anything else there for the rest of the game. ROW OR COLUMN COMPLETED ~If you circle all 5 items in a row or column, everyone else must X out everything that isn't already circled in that row or column. They can't circle anything more in that row or column for the rest of the game. JOKERS ~ The joker side of the die can never be used on its own. It must be combined with at least 1 other die. However, you can only use 1 joker per dice combo. EXAMPLE: You roll 2 jokers, 2 pink and 2 yellow. You can use 1 of the jokers with the 2 pink and 1 jokers with the 2 yellow. You CAN'T use the 2 jokers and the 2 pink together. Nor can you use just the 2 jokers on their own. If you roll ALL JOKERS, congratulations! Circle any item on your bookshelf :-) GAME END and SCORING When a player has no more items available in 2 rows (because they are circled and/or X'ed out), complete the round, then the game ends. Final scores are compared. IF you circled at AT LEAST 3 items in a row, score the points (the value shown in their top right corner) for all items circled in that row. IF you circled at AT LEAST 3 items in a column, score the points for all items circled in that column. Columns/rows with only 1 or 2 items circled earn no points! TIES: There is no tiebreaker ~ tied players share the victory.

[Rating: 1/10] Shares D.N.A. with both YAHTZEE and CAN'T STOP—more fun than the former for the fact that you can [i]somewhat[/i] strategically lock people out of columns/rows earlier than anticipated, but not as thrillingly push-your-luck as the latter. That said, I'd definitely reach for this before YAHTZEE, but that's a depressingly low bar to clear.

[Rating: 2/10] Fairly derivative dice checker.   Aiming for the high scores first seems to deliver the best results as nailing those to ensure big scores at the end takes time, plus the smaller combos can be picked up along the way. It’s important not to pin yourself into too tight a corner, but that is generic advice for all games of this type.  Overall there is nothing here that stands out against similar trifles.

[Rating: 3/10] I don't like roll and write games in the first place, but this one really seems like it brings nothing to the table for the genre. Perhaps I am missing an aspect of the strategy or the game is more fun at different player counts, but I did not feel engaged while playing as many turns were just a matter of picking the one correct/sensible option.

[Rating: 3/10] Simpler than Yahtzee, checking off boxes in a 5x5 array, where the farther right columns are harder to complete (need sets of X dice of the same icon to fill in a box in column X).  There's a race to fill in columns and rows (opponents have can't continue to score in a column or row after another player has finished it).  Doesn't add anything to the glut of roll and writes. I like roll/flip & writes, but these days if it's not simultaneous turns/piggybacking and plays high player counts, it's got to really offer something exciting to be worth my time.
